note: The detection results that moved from the M0 characterization (utils/detectLanguage.ts).
Not a folder of fixtures: these are hand-written texts, so the file name starts with an
underscore and the per-folder glob skips it.
Every fixture above answers exactly as it did at M0: only the cases below moved.
M8 (G10 review) adds the Okuma cases: an Okuma program under a Fanuc extension or under none at
all, which M0 read as Fanuc. The $NAME.MIN% header now decides wherever the file came from, and
the syntax only this control writes (a G71 thread cycle with H and D, a G77 tap with K, a line
that continues its block with $) outweighs the lines both lathes share. The Okuma fixtures
themselves are in okuma.json; these are the reviewer's own programs and two written for this case.
